utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case IT-99-36-PT, the Prosecutor against Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, I am Michael Keegan. I'm assisted by my colleague Ms. Anna Richterova, and we are further assisted by Ms. Ann Sutherland and Ms. Adele Erasmus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Keegan. For the accused, for Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is John Ackerman. I appear this morning on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pitron. I am going to ask each of the accused whether they are able to understand the proceedings in a language that they know. Mr. Brdjanin? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: General Talic? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. These proceedings are required by Rule 50(B) to enter fresh pleas to the amended indictment, in that it adds fresh charges. It is common practice within this Tribunal for the accused to waive his right to have the indictment read out in full before entering a plea. Mr. Ackerman, have you discussed that with your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, my client will waive the reading of the full indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Pitron, have you discussed this with your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Pitron, you do have to turn the microphone on each time, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. The answer, Judge, is no, my client does not wish to have the -- to waive the right to have the indictment read in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm not sure I follow what you're saying. Are you saying he does wish to have it read in full or he does waive his right to have it read in full?

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He waives the right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, I'll take each of the accused separately. Mr. Brdjanin, would you stand, please? In Count 1, you have been charged with genocide. Do you plead guilty or not guilty to that charge? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 2, you have been charged in complicity in genocide. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 3, you have been charged with a crime against humanity, being persecutions. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 4, you have been charged with a crime against humanity, being extermination. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 5, you have been charged with wilful killing as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 6, you have been charged with torture as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 7, you have been charged with torture as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 8, you have been charged with deportation as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 9, you have been charged with inhuman acts, being forcible transfer, as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 10, you have been charged with unlawful and wanton extensive destruction and appropriation of property not justified by military necessity as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions. Do you plea guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 11, you have been charged with a wanton destruction of cities, towns, or villages, or devastation not justified by military necessity as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 12, you have been charged with destruction or wilful damage done to institutions dedicated to religion as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brdjanin. You may sit down, please. General Talic, would you stand, please. In Count 1, you have been charged with genocide. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 2, you have been charged with complicity in genocide. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 3, you have been charged with persecutions as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 4, you have been charged with extermination as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 5, you have been charged with wilful killing as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 6, you have been charged with torture as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 7, you have been charged with torture as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 8, you've been charged with deportation as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 9, you have been charged with inhumane acts, being forcible transfer, as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 10, you have been charged with unlawful and wanton extensive destruction and appropriation of property not justified by military necessity as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 11, you have been charged with wanton destruction of cities, towns, or villages, or devastation not justified by military necessity as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In Count 12, you have been charged with destruction or wilful damage done to institutions dedicated to religion as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You may sit down, please, General Talic. Thank you. THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, I'd like to say a few sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, General Talic. THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] As far as I know, all the crimes that were done by military personnel in war are tried by military courts or international military courts or the warring states. This is logical and just because the military prosecution and military justice system is there to deal with the army and has the best knowledge of military organisation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: General Talic, you have to be translated and I think you're speaking very quickly. If you could just slow down a little bit, please. THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Would you like me to repeat what I have read out so far?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no. I think the translators have done a magnificent job in keeping up with you, but they were obviously labouring under some difficulty. If you would like to proceed. THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] I personally feel that justice and law would be satisfied only if I were to be tried by a military court of law; that is to say, Generals who have taken part in civil wars, and there are enough of them. Thank you, Your Honour, for allowing me to say a few words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, General Talic. You may sit down. Mr. Pitron, I don't know whether that is intended to constitute some challenge to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal. Is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Mr. Pitron, just one moment. We've got no English translation for that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear it now? Can you hear it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I can hear an English speaker now. I'm sorry, Mr. Pitron. Would you repeat what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to say, from a legal point of view, that we are not contesting the jurisdiction of the Tribunal in any way. On the other hand, I think that my client reacted quite personally, and after all, he's been in detention for almost four months now and he was not made familiar with the evidence upon which the indictment is based.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, thank you very much. I can I understand your client wishing to say something, but having said it, I propose to leave it where it stands, in the transcript.
